page: Amazon Web Services i7i.24xlarge is a storage-optimized instance engineered on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Compute is delivered by a dedicated 48-core, 96-thread Intel Xeon 8559C processor operating at 3.2 GHz across an x86_64 pipeline. It provides 768 GB of DDR5 system memory running at 6 GHz, allocating an 8 GB memory quotient per virtual core. Storage capabilities are anchored by 22,500 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD space, backed by a baseline network interface speed of 56 Gbps. The processor features a 320 MB L3 cache alongside specialized instruction sets including Intel AMX for matrix operations and AVX-512 extensions.

Benchmark testing positions this instance in the top decile for heavy multi-core throughput and data ingestion. It recorded a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,887.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 93,054.5. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 552.44 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput scaled to 132.74 GB/sec. Uncached memory read bandwidth maintained 287.02 GB/sec. In transactional caching environments, the platform sustained 113.26 million Redis SET operations per second and registered a score of 32,606.17 on PassMark database tests.

Integrating 22.5 TB of low-latency NVMe SSD storage inside the instance provides strong resource efficiency by removing the network overhead and separate capacity costs typical of remote block volumes. Because the system contains no dedicated graphics accelerators, text generation during large language model inference is constrained, producing 4.95 tokens per second on 70B models. The hardware profile is aligned with high-performance transactional databases, distributed datastores such as Apache Cassandra, real-time analytics engines, in-memory caching layers, and search indexing.
description: Amazon Web Services i7i.24xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring an Intel Xeon 8559C x86_64 processor with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at 3.2 GHz. The platform is configured with 768 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz and 22,500 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, supplemented by a 56 Gbps baseline network interface. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-tier multi-threaded compute results, demonstrated by a PassMark CPU score of 93,054.5 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,887.0, along with sustaining 113.26 million Redis SET operations per second. The dense aggregation of high-capacity local storage and large memory reserves offers significant cost efficiency for I/O-intensive workloads without relying on external network storage. It lacks GPU accelerators, making it best fitted for large-scale transactional databases, distributed storage systems, data warehousing, and high-throughput real-time analytics.
